audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for later departures, false asceticism, creation goodness, training in reverence, youth, public reading/teaching, gift.

verses.restored: But the Spirit expressly says that in later seasons some will depart from the trust, paying attention to misleading spirits and teachings of daimons,

familiar.text: Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;

modern.text: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons,

original.text: Τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ῥητῶς λέγει ὅτι ἐν ὑστέροις καιροῖς ἀποστήσονταί τινες τῆς πίστεως, προσέχοντες πνεύμασι πλάνοις καὶ διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων

verses.restored: in hypocrisy of false-speakers, having been seared in their own conscience,

familiar.text: Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;

modern.text: influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.

original.text: ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων, κεκαυστηριασμένων τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν,

verses.restored: forbidding to marry, commanding abstinence from foods that the Divine created to be received with thanksgiving by those trusting and knowing the truth.

familiar.text: Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.

modern.text: They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.

original.text: κωλυόντων γαμεῖν, ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἔκτισεν εἰς μετάλημψιν μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ ἐπεγνωκόσι τὴν ἀλήθειαν.

verses.restored: Because every creature/created thing of the Divine is beautiful/good, and nothing is to be rejected when received with thanksgiving,

familiar.text: For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:

modern.text: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,

original.text: ὅτι πᾶν κτίσμα θεοῦ καλόν, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπόβλητον μετὰ εὐχαριστίας λαμβανόμενον,

verses.restored: for it is sanctified through word of Divine and prayer.

familiar.text: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.

modern.text: because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer. A Good Servant of Jesus Christ

original.text: ἁγιάζεται γὰρ διὰ λόγου θεοῦ καὶ ἐντεύξεως.

verses.restored: Putting these things before the siblings, you will be a beautiful/good servant of Messiah Jesus, being nourished in the words of the trust and of the beautiful/good teaching that you have followed.

familiar.text: If thou put the brethren in remembrance of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine, whereunto thou hast attained.

modern.text: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.

original.text: Ταῦτα ὑποτιθέμενος τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καλὸς ἔσῃ διάκονος ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃, ἐντρεφόμενος τοῖς λόγοις τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς καλῆς διδασκαλίας ᾗ παρηκολούθηκας,

verses.restored: But profane and old-womanish myths refuse; train yourself toward reverence/godliness.

familiar.text: But refuse profane and old wives’ fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.

modern.text: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.

original.text: τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ. γύμναζε δὲ σεαυτὸν πρὸς εὐσέβειαν·

verses.restored: For bodily training is beneficial for a little, but reverence/godliness is beneficial for all things, having promise of life now and of the coming one.

familiar.text: For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.

modern.text: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.

original.text: ἡ γὰρ σωματικὴ γυμνασία πρὸς ὀλίγον ἐστὶν ὠφέλιμος, ἡ δὲ εὐσέβεια πρὸς πάντα ὠφέλιμός ἐστιν, ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχουσα ζωῆς τῆς νῦν καὶ τῆς μελλούσης.

verses.restored: Trustworthy is the saying and worthy of full welcome.

familiar.text: This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.

modern.text: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.

original.text: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος,

verses.restored: For into this we labor and struggle, because we have hoped upon living Divine, who is Savior/Healer of all humans, especially of trusting ones.

familiar.text: For therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.

modern.text: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.

original.text: εἰς τοῦτο ⸀γὰρ κοπιῶμεν καὶ ⸀ὀνειδιζόμεθα, ὅτι ἠλπίκαμεν ἐπὶ θεῷ ζῶντι, ὅς ἐστιν σωτὴρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων, μάλιστα πιστῶν.

verses.restored: Let no one despise your youth, but become a pattern for the trusting ones in word, in conduct, in love, in trust, in purity.

familiar.text: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.

modern.text: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

original.text: μηδείς σου τῆς νεότητος καταφρονείτω, ἀλλὰ τύπος γίνου τῶν πιστῶν ἐν λόγῳ, ἐν ἀναστροφῇ, ἐν ⸀ἀγάπῃ, ἐν πίστει, ἐν ἁγνείᾳ.

verses.restored: Until I come, pay attention to the public reading, to the encouragement/appeal, to the teaching.

familiar.text: Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.

modern.text: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.

original.text: ἕως ἔρχομαι πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει, τῇ παρακλήσει, τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ.

verses.restored: Do not neglect the grace-gift in you, which was given to you through prophecy with laying on of the hands of the council of elders.

familiar.text: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

modern.text: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.

original.text: μὴ ἀμέλει τοῦ ἐν σοὶ χαρίσματος, ὃ ἐδόθη σοι διὰ προφητείας μετὰ ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου.

verses.restored: Practice these things; be in them, so that your progress may be manifest to all.

familiar.text: Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.

modern.text: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.

original.text: ταῦτα μελέτα, ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι, ἵνα σου ἡ προκοπὴ φανερὰ ⸀ᾖ πᾶσιν·

verses.restored: Pay attention to yourself and to the teaching; remain in them. For doing this, you will save/heal both yourself and those hearing you.

familiar.text: Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.

modern.text: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

original.text: ἔπεχε σεαυτῷ καὶ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ· ἐπίμενε αὐτοῖς· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν καὶ σεαυτὸν σώσεις καὶ τοὺς ἀκούοντάς σου.

translation_notes: The anti-ascetic section is body/creation-positive: created things are good and received with thanksgiving.
Bodily training is not rejected; it is relativized beside reverence/godliness.
Daimons is transliterated in notes as hostile spiritual teachings without overdeveloping later demonology.
